items.title: feat(id): F12.9 program upgrade with state migration and rollback (#1066)
items.body: ## F12.9 program upgrade with state migration and rollback (#1066) Implements the confirmed F12.9 remainder for task 12962, now that the gate has landed: issue #1065 (F12.8 guest SDKs) closed via PR #7891 (merged 2026-11-09T01:03Z), verified fresh at claim time. Before this PR, `pkgs/id/src/world/` had no upgrade module, no migrate export, no versioned program-state snapshot format, and no upgrade runner. ### What lands New module `pkgs/id/src/world/upgrade.rs`, re-exported from `crate::world`: - **Versioned snapshot format for world program state** — `ProgramSnapshot` with a magic + format-version envelope. Format v1 (magic, one version byte, raw state) is still decoded so old snapshots upgrade; everything new is encoded at the current format v2 (version, state length, state, FNV-1a checksum), and the decoded snapshot records the format version it was read from. - **Optional `migrate` export in the guest ABI** — the `MigrateExport` host-side contract: `migrate(state, from_version, to_version) -> Result`. Programs without the export (`None`) keep working under the pre-existing behavior: their state is carried across the upgrade byte-for-byte. - **Probe-first upgrade runner** — `upgrade_program` decodes and migrates a probe copy of the state, re-encodes it at the current snapshot format, and reads it back; the running program's version and snapshot are swapped only if the migrated state round-trips exactly. Any failure (migrate refuses, migrated state over the 4 MiB bound, round-trip mismatch) leaves the old program bit-for-bit unchanged — that is the rollback. ### Exit tests (plan, Phase 12 F12.9) In-module tests, each naming its oracle: - `counter_upgrades_across_a_snapshot_format_change` — a v1 ASCII-decimal counter in a v1 snapshot upgrades to a v2 little-endian counter in a current-format snapshot, same value. - `failing_upgrade_leaves_the_old_program_running` — a deliberately failing `migrate` leaves version and snapshot bytes unchanged. - Plus: current-format round-trip records its version, legacy v1 snapshots still decode, corrupted snapshots are refused, no-`migrate` programs carry state unchanged, oversized migrated state rolls back. Targeted tests run on the laptop before opening (`cargo test --lib world::upgrade`: 7 passed); full verification is CI per fleet policy. ### Scope notes - No F12.8 work (issue #1065, landed separately) and no F12.15 work (issue #558, the downstream consumer of this migration path). - The runner is the transport-independent core seam (alongside the BUILDER-gated program install/upgrade path in `world/mod.rs`); wiring it into a live hot-swap command is follow-up work, not hidden in this PR. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(id): program ecosystem (share, fork, gallery) first-pass design (#6278)
items.body:
## Summary

First-pass research + design record for the Phase-14 Program ecosystem core topic: doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/.

- D1 program identity = (author public key, name, version, content hash); same-version/different-hash is a surfaced provenance violation
- D2 the signed bundle (per F12.17 #1069, ABI descriptor per F12.7 #1064) is the unit of travel; sideloading always works, fully offline
- D3 fork lineage is structural and cumulative in the bundle — attribution cannot be stripped without breaking provenance
- D4 install/update authority: pinned by default; updates beyond the F12.7/F12.9 no-approval envelope need explicit world-owner approval
- D5 template worlds strip members, credentials, per-user data, and grants by default, recorded in the template manifest
- D6 the gallery is a plural registry protocol (big server / pkarr / self-host, one record, over iroh); validity is protocol, admission is operator policy
- 7 invariants, 5 alternatives rejected, and the v1-v4 ladder (#6291, #6293, #6294, #6295) mapped; this record meets the v1 entry condition

## Implementation issues filed from the record

- #8280 — signed program bundle format + sideload import
- #8281 — gallery registry protocol + reference registry service
- #8282 — template-world snapshot export/import

## Evidence

- Verification: npx prettier --check on the new doc + doc/README.md — pass; git diff --check — pass (docs-only change)
- Foundations re-verified fresh this shift: #1064, #1065, #1066, #1069, #1061 CLOSED; #6291/#6293/#6294/#6295 OPEN as the ladder; no pre-existing bundle/gallery/template implementation issues (GitHub search, 2026-11-10)

Closes #6278

items.title: feat(id): fixture replay as a promotion gate for id world dev (#5541 phase 3)

labels.name: audit:completed-later
labels.description: Gap completed by later merged PR

items.body: Phase 3 of the F12.15 `id world dev` authoring loop (design `doc/2026-11-01_design_id558.md`, issue #5541): fixture replay as a promotion gate. Task 14893, lane code-b. Phase 1 landed in PR #8153; the design's Phase-2 gate (F12.9, issue #1066) is now closed, and this slice is independent of the watch machinery — in the one-shot loop, promotion is launch/no-launch. Phases 2, 4, 5 remain and convert to a follow-on task. ## What - `id world dev --fixture FILE` (repeatable): each fixture is read (bounded, like `replay`) and decoded, then replayed against the compiled candidate **before launch** (`world_dev::fixture_gate`). - The gate is the design's dev-only cross-module-hash regression mode (invariant 5): `check_module` is deliberately not called, so a fixture recorded under an earlier module hash still replays; the gate result reports `cross_module`. Ordinary `replay`/`verify` stay strict — untouched. - A fixture whose replayed records mismatch its recorded expectation **blocks promotion**: the candidate is not launched, no input is applied, the JSON report carries `promoted: false` with the gate results, and the command exits non-zero naming the mismatching fixture(s). - Partial fixtures replay their retained window; a fixture with no recorded expectation, or one whose final epoch is not covered, reports `not_compared` with the reason instead of silently passing. A fixture recording no active module, or holding an unreplayable event kind, fails the command with a diagnostic naming the fixture. - `DevReport` gains `fixture_gates` and `promoted`; `DevScratchWorld` gains a `records()` accessor (the live-records oracle the gate tests build fixtures from, and a seam Phase 2 needs). ## Tests (oracle: the live counter world's own records) - `cargo test --lib world_dev::` — 8 passed: the 4 pre-existing plus `fixture_gate_promotes_a_candidate_that_reproduces_the_fixture`, `fixture_gate_blocks_a_candidate_whose_records_diverge`, `fixture_gate_replays_a_fixture_recorded_under_another_module`, `fixture_gate_reports_a_fixture_with_no_expectation`. - `cargo test --lib -- world` — 699 + 83 passed, 0 failed. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(id): program ecosystem v2 design — gallery & updates (#6293)
items.body: ## What Lands the v2 design record for the Phase 14 Program ecosystem ladder step #6293 (gallery & updates): `doc/2026-11-11T05-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem_v2/`. The record refines core decision D6 (the gallery is a registry, and registries are plural) and D4 (install semantics and update authority) for the v2 slice only, on top of the core record (`doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/`, PR #8288) and the v1 record (`doc/2026-11-11T05-01-15Z_design_id_program_ecosystem_v1/`, PR #8541): - Registry record format: one protocol, two object types (bundle records, template records); validity is protocol (hash/signature verified at ingest and read), admission is operator policy. - Three publishing paths (hosted / pkarr / self-hosted) carrying the identical record; publish and withdrawal are author speech (signed), delisting and annotations are registry/operator speech, never presented as author data. - Update channels: a channel is one author's (author key, name) version line; the install record's policy field (`pinned` default, `tracking` opt-in) goes live; a fork is a different line — lineage is history, not a channel. - Update flow: v1 import verification first, then the D4 approval envelope (same ABI, no capability widening, F12.9 migration), a fixed approval summary including the author's signed changelog, and F12.9 rollback as part of the apply act. - Seven invariants, each naming its test oracle; v2 refusal taxonomy additions; open questions explicitly deferred (template index layout to #8281, push notification to v3 policy). Implementation breakdown (design record §11, linked from #6293 and #6278): #8281 (gallery registry protocol + reference registry, already filed) and #8546 (program update channels + update flow, filed with this record — the one v2 item no earlier issue owned). Docs only; no implementation code, per the #6293 charter. ## Verification - `prettier --check` on the new record: passes. - `git diff --check`: passes. - Entry condition verified fresh 2026-11-11: #6291 CLOSED with the v1 design landed (PR #8541); #6278 CLOSED; F12.7 #1064, F12.9 #1066, F12.10 #1067, F12.17 #1069 CLOSED. items.title: feat(id): id world dev phase 1 — one-shot local compile + disposable scratch world (#5541)

labels.name: audit:completed-later
labels.description: Gap completed by later merged PR

items.body: Implements **Phase 1** of the F12.15 `id world dev` authoring loop for #5541 (design: `doc/2026-11-01_design_id558.md`). The design's dependency gate is now satisfied — F12.9 #1066 landed via #8031 and F12.8 #1065 is closed — verified fresh this shift before starting. ## What this slice does - **`id world dev DIR`** (sandbox feature): source discovery for an app directory (`main.roc` first, sibling `.roc` files in name order, size-capped reads, validated by the compiler's own bounds), platform resolution from `main.roc`'s declared platform path (or `--platform`), and compilation through the existing bounded compiler engine (`world_compile::compile`). A local dev session grants every module its platform provides; hosted worlds keep their capability ceilings. - **Disposable scratch world**: the compiled module launches into an in-memory `WorldCore` + `WorldHandle` with a sandbox guest — the design's chosen local actor seam. No host is contacted, nothing is installed into a named world, and the scratch state is discarded when the session ends. - `--input TEXT` (repeatable) sends inputs as the dev guest; the command prints one JSON report: source files, seed, module size, compiler diagnostics, source-build provenance, initial view, view after each input, records sequence. ## Verification - `cargo test --lib -- world_dev test_cli_parse_world_dev` — **5 passed** on the laptop. The lifecycle test is the disposability oracle: the checked-in Roc counter starts at `count=0`, applies `inc` inputs through the actor to `count=2`, and a fresh launch starts again at `count=0`. - New module is `rustfmt`-clean; CLI parse test covers the new subcommand. ## Known gap (pre-existing, not this PR) An end-to-end compile of a Roc app cannot run on the laptop today: the platform host build (`examples/roc-world/build-host.sh`) fails on the installed Zig 0.17 (`Optimize.Debug` removed), so `targets/wasm32/host.wasm` cannot be produced. Filed as **#8152**. The compile leg here reuses `world_compile::compile`, which the host `Compile` path already exercises; once #8152 lands, `id world dev pkgs/id/examples/roc-counter --input inc` is the e2e check. ## Follow-ups (later design phases, staying on #5541) Watch/debounce + F12.9 hot-swap via `world::upgrade`, fixture promotion gates (dev-only cross-module-hash replay), deterministic fuzz + declared invariants, latency benchmark + authoring docs. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added `id world dev` for compiling and running an app locally in an offline, disposable environment. * Specify an app directory and optionally a platform, Roc compiler, seed, and ordered text inputs. * View the initial state and the result after each input in a JSON report.

items.title: fix(agy-proxy): flush unterminated tail line before judging no-output on close (#683)
items.body: Fixes #683 (triage task 1066 confirmed on main; queue task 4595). ## What `AgyWorker`'s close handler judged a failed turn before ever looking at `lineBuffer`: a final `step_update` delta that arrived without a trailing newline was invisible, so `_fail` set `hasOutput=false` and the resume-retry gate (`allowRetry && resumed && !err.hasOutput`) silently retried the turn as a fresh conversation, discarding the partial output. - The close handler now calls `_flushLineBuffer()` first: the unterminated tail runs through the exact same per-line path (`_processLine`, extracted from `_onStdout`) as a terminated line — delta delivered / result handled — before `_fail` judges output. - No other behaviour change: a genuinely output-free failed resume still retries fresh (existing #678 test unchanged and passing). ## Tests - New stub case `FAILTAIL` (resumed conversation emits an unterminated `partial tail` delta, then exits 3) + regression test: non-stream 502 with the stub's stderr, stream delivers the `partial tail` delta chunk then an error event, never a `stop`. - Regression validity: with the pristine proxy the new test fails (10/11 pass); with this fix the full file passes 11/11 (`node --test bin/agy-proxy.test.mjs`, run on the laptop with the stub reachable — note the laptop's system `agy` at `/run/current-system/sw/bin/agy` shadows the test stub in-place, a pre-existing environment quirk that makes the unmodified suite fail identically on clean main; CI does not have that shadow). --- Need help on this PR? items.title: id(sync): split serve range sessions onto /id-range-sync/1 (#179)
items.body: Fix for #179 (queue task 2970) — both halves, so #179 closes with this PR. ## What changed **1. The split (earlier commits).** `serve`'s range sessions (`event_store::sync`, via `EventSyncProtocol`) opened with a range flight on `/id-sync/1` — the same ALPN as `log_sync` sessions whose first frame is a `Request`/`Answer` handshake, so each side misread the other. Range sessions moved to a distinct ALPN, **`/id-range-sync/1`**, with the split documented in code and in `doc/2026-10-29T16-21-00Z_design_id_sync_alpn_split/`. **2. Range under the handshake (00569c4b).** `log_sync::run_agreed` no longer returns `NotWired` for `SyncMethod::Range`: a Range request agreed under the `Request`/`Answer` handshake now runs a range session on the same stream pair. The store seam is **per-call locking** — the range session is generalised over a new `event_store::sync::RangeStore` trait (sync set / one event's bytes / one ingest batch); `SharedEventStore` takes its `RwLock` per step, never across an await, the same discipline the range session already used internally. The handshake itself now runs on the raw streams; only the `Log` arm wraps them in `Frames`. `sync_method` gains `LogAndRange` support — `LogSyncOnly` responders still refuse Range, and refusal/mismatch semantics are unchanged. `SyncError::NotWired` is removed. Design record: `doc/2026-10-29T16-57-03Z_design_id_sync_range_store_seam/`. New tests: one peer/store pair syncs by Log then by Range under the one handshake (both sides report the agreed method, stores converge after each); a first frame that is not a valid `Request` is refused as a frame error; `LogAndRange` supports both methods. ## Verification CI on this PR (no local builds per fleet CI-first rule). Known blockers unrelated to this change: `main` fmt/clippy breakage fixed by #2335, and the merge-queue stall #1599 — this PR merges once those clear. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Range synchronization can now run through the shared sync handshake when both sides support it. * Sync results distinguish stored-but-voided events from applied events. * **Bug Fixes** * Events refused because a store is frozen are counted as refused, not voided. * **Compatibility** * Range sessions served by `id serve` now use `/id-range-sync/1`; log synchronization continues to use `/id-sync/1`. * **Documentation** * Updated protocol and serving documentation to reflect the distinction between range and log synchronization.

items.title: fix(mcpx): delimiter scanner — 4 further heuristic false-positive shapes (#3346)
items.body: Fixes #3346 — the 4 further heuristic false-positive shapes the Codex review of PR #3339 found in `checkSyntaxAndDelimiters` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/scripting/validator.go`), each fixed with regression tests in `TestValidationRegexLiteralsAreOpaque`: 1. **Relational chain with a regex operand** — `1 < Number > /[)]/.source.length`: the instantiation-expression speculation no longer fires when the operand before `<` is a numeric or string literal (neither can bear a generic argument list), so the `>` stays relational and the slash opens the regex. 2. **Nested statement blocks in heritage operands** — `class C extends {C: function(){ {} /[}]/.test('}'); }}.C {}`: heritage braces are now marked per-brace on the delimiter stack; a pending function/class expression body (or declaration body) that opens inside an open heritage brace is a body, not another heritage operand, and braces nested inside it classify by the ordinary rules. Arrow bodies are likewise never heritage operands. 3. **Escaped identifiers at a line start** — `let a=1;\n\u0061++ / 2;`: the Unicode-escape consumption path now consumes a pending line break like an ordinary identifier character, so the `++`/`--` reads as a postfix on the escaped identifier instead of a prefix. 4. **Property named `new` before an ASI declaration** — `obj.new\nclass C {}`: `isExprPositionStart` now receives the significant character before the previous identifier (`prevIdentPrev`) and applies the same member-access guard used elsewhere, so a property named like an expression keyword no longer makes a following function/class declaration read as an expression. Verification: `go test ./internal/scripting/ -count=1` passes on the laptop (full suite, incl. the 6 new regression subtests and the division controls `a / b / c`, `x /= 2`, unclosed delimiter/string after division). `gofmt` clean. Queue task 5059 (lane F). --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved script validation when distinguishing regular expressions from division across spread operands, TypeScript instantiations, Unicode identifiers, comments, and nested class heritage expressions. * Improved handling of escaped identifiers and TypeScript instantiations following numeric values. * **Tests** * Added coverage for these validation cases, including scripts with large numbers of block comments.

items.title: mcpx: dependency configuration chain, slice 1 — deps.* settings, paths.deps, ExecOptions.deps (#1913)
items.body: Slice 1 of #1913 (queue task 3191): the dependency configuration chain's configuration + transport half. Follow-up of the design/analysis on #1913; remaining slice-1 items (runner emission, plugin parity) are listed at the bottom. ## What this slice does - **Settings**: `deps.*` group (source, manifest, autoInstall, frozen, + `paths.deps`) declared in the settings registry and read through accessors; `docs/configuration.md` / `docs/environment.md` regenerated. - **`internal/deps`**: `Config`/`From`, scope-aware `Parse`, `Conflicts`, manifest Find/Load/walk-up, JSONC stripping, the `Set`/`Resolve` chain, `Frozen`, `Describe`, and JSON/lockfile text forms — with chain tests. - **Transport**: `execsvc.Options.Deps` (+ `DepsOptions`) carries the dependency set as *text, not paths* (a path would name the caller's filesystem); CLI `a.depsOptions` wired into the exec and run wire paths, with CLI tests. ## Tests Laptop: `go test ./internal/deps/ ./internal/execsvc/` pass; `internal/settings` shows only the two failures that also fail on clean origin/main (verified in a detached worktree at origin/main): `TestTheReadByColumnIsWhatTheCodeReads`, `TestEveryDocumentHasAChapter`. Full `go test ./...` runs in CI. ## Remaining (tracked on task 3191's checkpoint) - internal/runner emission: deno `npm:` specifiers / deno.json imports map; bun/node materialised package.json in the exec workdir; frozen lockfile honoured (bun --frozen-lockfile / npm ci / deno.lock), never rewriting a user project; autoInstall → `--install=` mapping. - Flag reach: `Commands: runCommands` on the deps settings so `--deps-source/--deps-manifest/--deps-autoInstall/--paths-deps` reach run+exec (flagreach parity test). - Plugin parity check for Deps on the exec path. - `docs/proposals.md` "Modules and libraries" status truth-up. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Configure script dependencies with package requests, project manifests, and dependency paths. * Choose dependency sources and whether supported runtimes install dependencies automatically. * Dependencies and relevant lockfiles are prepared for script execution, including local package references and runtime-specific lockfile selection. * Manifest discovery can use the script’s directory, and JSONC manifests are supported. * **Bug Fixes** * Conflicting package versions are reported as errors instead of proceeding with incompatible dependency requests. * **Documentation** * Added reference material for dependency settings and their behavior.
